simulacao.02: You will get a lot wrong at the start. That was never the problem.
simulacao.03: People learning chart analysis are right about half the time. That is normal, and it is nothing to be ashamed of — it is the price of learning to read a chart. What breaks a beginner's bankroll is not the hit rate. It is what they do after the fourth loss in a row.
simulacao.04: At an 87% payout, every $1 lost costs $1.15 to win back. Four losses demand five wins, and five wins in a row show up only 10.9% of the time. That distance is what makes the hand rise on its own and double the entry.
simulacao.05: So we measured it. We simulated 200,000 sessions using Gerenciador PRO's own settings: a $10,000 bankroll, a 2% entry, a 10% target, a 15% stop loss and an 87% payout. At a 50% hit rate, a flat entry reaches the target in 35.4% of sessions. Recovery Cycles reach it in 49.3%.
simulacao.06: And classic martingale? It reaches the target more often still — 63%. But when it fails it ends at $7,000: 30% down, twice the 15% stop loss the trader had set. Gerenciador PRO stops at $7,957. The difference is not how often you win. It is the size of the damage when you lose.
simulacao.07: Doubling after a loss walks straight through the limit you set for yourself. That is the real danger, and it is invisible until the session it isn't.
simulacao.08: No money management invents profit, and anyone promising you that is lying. At a 50% hit rate every average here ends below the starting bankroll. And once you reach 60%, a flat entry overtakes everything else. Gerenciador PRO was built for the beginning — that is where it changes the outcome most.
simulacao.09: Sessions reaching the target with a flat entry
simulacao.10: Sessions reaching the target with Gerenciador PRO
simulacao.11: The conditions these numbers were calculated under
simulacao.12: Bankroll of $10,000. Entry of 2%, target of +10%, stop loss of −15%, payout of 87%, recovery split 35/65 across the two entries. Hit rate of 50%, the equivalent of a coin. 200,000 sessions simulated for each system, following the exact rules of the app: the second entry of a hand is only played after the first one wins.
simulacao.13: The figures are proportional: a $1,000 bankroll with a $20 entry produces exactly the same percentages. What matters is the ratio between entry and bankroll, not the currency or the size.
simulacao.14: Results change with the settings. A wider stop loss lets recovery run longer and raises both the chance of reaching the target and the size of the worst sessions.
simulacao.16: A tool for organisation and operational control. It does not promise, suggest or guarantee financial results. Simulations do not predict future outcomes.
